The driver himself admits he left the booked optimal corridor. His own in-app message to the rider at 11:29:04 reads 'boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?', and his counterparty statement confirms 'I came off and used Upper Thomson.' That is a party statement placing the vehicle off the BKE optimal route, so the factual premise of the rider's complaint - that this trip did not follow the optimal route - is admitted by the driver, not merely asserted by the rider.

The driver's traffic explanation is unsupported by any artifact. The only advisory in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00102-01, is empty: it carries no payload at all, so no advisory names a road the optimal route traverses, gives no validity window and supplies no shortest_lawful_alternative_km. I rely here on an artifact with no payload, which under POL-GEN-02 carries weight 0.0 and can carry no fact. Under POL-RD-08 the burden is on the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge it. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable to the driver.

The record triggers mandatory escalation under POL-RD-10(5). The driver asserts an external traffic obstruction on the optimal route - 'BKE had a slow crawl near Dairy Farm' - which is a POL-RD-03 exculpatory assertion, and the artifact that clause requires, the traffic_advisory, is in the pool only as EV-ADVIS-00102-01 with no payload, i.e. a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0. POL-RD-10(5) names precisely this configuration, 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory', and directs that no final ruling issue and the case escalate, with the disputed amount held rather than collected. Because this is a rider-filed dispute, a NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 would leave the contested charge standing against the rider, whereas escalation holds it and is the outcome the rider seeks on this record.

No extra corroboration is demanded of this rider by POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 2 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, which is below the four-claims and one-substantiated trigger, so the clause's additional-corroboration requirement for sub-30% claims is not engaged and cannot be used to discount this claim.

I must be candid, because stretching this point would cost the brief. On the governing trace figure the excess is 1.39 km - 6.8% of the 20.4 km optimal distance - which clears the 0.8 km absolute gate but falls well short of the 20% proportional gate (4.08 km). POL-RD-01 requires both tests to pass, and where either fails it directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, save for a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4); and the fare breakdown shows no phantom gantry and no airport surcharge, so that route is closed too. The rider's factual complaint is borne out by the driver's admission, but the distance gate is not crossed on this trip's own numbers, and I do not pretend otherwise.

claims.text: Under POL-RD-01 a route deviation is ESTABLISHED only when the excess is both greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; both tests must pass. The GPS-derived excess on this trip is 1.39 km against an optimal route of 20.4 km, i.e. 6.81%. That is far below the 20% gate. The percentage test fails, so no deviation exists on this trip and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the route he expected the driver to take.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing distance and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test, because it is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. The governing trace figure is 21.79 km; the rounded copy is 21.8 km. Measured on the governing figure the excess is still only 1.39 km, or 6.81% of the 20.4 km optimal route, so the trace-governs rule does not rescue the rider's claim - it confirms it fails either way.

Even on the rider's own account the excess (1.39 km, 6.81%) sits well below both materiality gates in POL-RD-01 - 50% of optimal or 8.0 km absolute - so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged. Were it run, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 640 completed_trips_90d in the same window (0%, against a 3-flag or 5% threshold), so no repeat-deviation pattern can be established and no adverse finding attaches to this driver.

POL-RD-08 puts the initial burden on the rider: he must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess that meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace here is unimpaired (100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap 0 seconds) and it shows an excess that fails the percentage gate, so the burden is never discharged. The driver therefore need not reach any exculpatory clause, and the rider's assertions carry no weight to the extent they cite no artifact.

POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative: it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand. On this record payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so a NO_ACTION outcome leaves the metered charge of $29.91 in place and the rider's contested $7.00 is not returned. Because this dispute was filed by the rider, NO_ACTION is a clean outcome for the driver.

POL-RD-09(4) makes a billing-integrity refund available whether or not a deviation exists, but there is nothing to correct here: fare_breakdown.erp_gantries is an empty set, tolls and ERP total 0.00, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport. No phantom gantry, no off-route pass-through charge and no wrongly applied surcharge can be found on this fare, so the rider's only residual route to a refund is closed.

The only chat message on the trip is the driver's own, sent in-app at 11:29:04 - 'boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?' - an open notification of the route choice six minutes into a completed trip, with no rider reply or objection recorded in the log. That is inconsistent with the rider's account of a covert roundabout detour, and the disclosed route change is in any event measured by the trace at a 1.39 km excess, which does not meet the POL-RD-01 threshold.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver:

What was claimed. The rider says the driver left the BKE for Mandai/Upper Thomson, that the trip took 32 minutes against a normal 27, and asks for $7.00 of the $29.91 metered fare back.

That the route changed is not really in dispute. The driver's own in-app message at 11:29:04 ("boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?") and his statement confirm he came off the booked corridor. But a route change is only a refundable deviation if it clears the gate in POL-RD-01, and this one does not.

The numbers. The governing distance is the GPS trace figure, not the trip record's rounded copy: trace_distance_km is 21.79 km (EV-GPS-00102), against the booked optimal of 20.4 km (EV-TRIP-00102, optimal_distance_km). The excess is 1.39 km, or 6.81% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be both more than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND more than 20% of the optimal distance (20% of 20.4 km is 4.08 km). The absolute test passes at 1.39 km; the proportional test fails at 6.81% against 4.08 km. Both must pass, so no deviation is established and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. Measuring on the trip record's 21.8 km copy gives the same 6.81% and the same result, which is why the trace-governs rule does not change the outcome.

Driver. Your traffic explanation ("BKE had a slow crawl near Dairy Farm") could only have mattered if a deviation had been established and you had invoked POL-RD-03 with a traffic advisory naming the affected road and a validity window. You cited no evidence ID and no clause, and under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad does not discharge the burden. The only advisory in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00102-01, carries no payload and can support no fact; it changes nothing here, because the deviation gate was never crossed and the exculpatory route was never reached.

Rider. I have considered and rejected your escalation argument. POL-RD-10(5) fires only where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool or lacks the field the clause requires. Here no clause was invoked and no artifact was cited; a bare traffic assertion is discarded under POL-RD-08, and POL-RD-03 was never reached because no deviation exists. No other POL-RD-10 trigger applies: the trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, 193 fixes, max gap 0 s), the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown (TRP-00102), the timestamps are consistent (requested 11:16:40, started 11:23:30, ended 11:55:30), and every fare line matches the trip record (base $3.80 + distance $16.35 + time $8.96 + platform fee $0.80 = $29.91).

Billing integrity. Nothing to correct under POL-RD-09(4): ERP and tolls are $0.00, no gantries were charged, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge.

Pattern. The driver's record shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days against 640 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no POL-RD-06 referral arises. No other clause produces a referral.

Outcome. NO_ACTION. No part of the contested $7.00 is refunded, the metered charge of $29.91 stands (payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd $0.00 are left as they are), and no compensation is payable to the driver. Confidence 0.90.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the claim is not upheld and the metered charge of $29.91 stands.

WHAT IS NOT IN DISPUTE. Both sides agree about this trip. TRP-00102 ran from Woodlands to ION Orchard on 19 July 2026. The platform's optimal route was 20.4 km / 27 minutes; the trip took 32 minutes. The rider's identity burden under POL-RD-08(a) is met: the trip id TRP-00102 is carried unchanged on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first fix (11:23:30) matches the trip record's started_at.

THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT. Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the GPS trace figure, not the rounded copy on the trip record. The trace (EV-GPS-00102, 100% coverage, 193 fixes, no gaps, max gap 0 s) measures 21.79 km against an optimal 20.4 km, so the excess is 1.39 km, or 6.81% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km. The absolute gate is cleared (1.39 km > 0.8 km), but the proportional gate is not: 20% of 20.4 km is 4.08 km, and 1.39 km falls well short. Because one of the two tests fails, POL-RD-01 directs that no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. Both advocates reached this conclusion, and the rider's advocate is right to concede it.

THE DRIVER'S ROUTE CHANGE. I accept that the driver left the booked corridor. His own in-app message at 11:29:04 ('boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?') and his statement ('BKE had a slow crawl near Dairy Farm so I came off and used Upper Thomson') show a deliberate switch to Upper Thomson. That finding does not change the result: a route change is refundable only if it produces an excess crossing both POL-RD-01 gates, and on this trip's own numbers it did not.

ESCALATION IS NOT WARRANTED. The rider's advocate asks for escalation under POL-RD-10(5), on the ground that the driver asserted a traffic obstruction and the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00102-01, has a null payload. I do not accept that. POL-RD-10(5) applies where a party INVOKES an exculpatory clause against an artifact that is missing or defective. The driver never invokes POL-RD-03 - his case is that the threshold fails - and a general assertion that traffic was bad, citing no evidence ID, carries no weight and is discarded under POL-RD-08 rather than escalated. The empty advisory is in any event immaterial: with or without a closure, the excess is 1.39 km and no deviation is established, so a human reviewer would have nothing to resolve. For completeness: EV-ADVIS-00102-01 carries no payload and can carry no fact, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on it; that does not affect this ruling.

THE FARE AND THE OTHER ROUTES. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00102) is METERED, charged_total $29.91, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd $0.00. The POL-RD-02 arithmetic would give a recomputed fare of $27.46 and a refund of $2.45 if a deviation had been established, but none was, so no refund runs. The billing-integrity route under POL-RD-09(4) is closed: erp_gantries is empty, ERP and tolls total $0.00, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no phantom line or wrongly applied surcharge to refund. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged because the deviation is not MATERIAL (1.39 km against materiality gates of 8.0 km or 50%); and in any case driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 640 completed trips in the window, so no repeat pattern is established and no conduct referral arises. No referral is made on any clause.

CONFIDENCE. The deciding facts - the trace distance and the platform optimal distance - are carried by EV-GPS-00102 and EV-TRIP-00102 at full weight, and the trace is unimpaired at policy level under POL-RD-07. Nothing below full weight carries the ruling. Confidence 0.90.

OUTCOME. NO_ACTION: this is a rider-filed dispute, so the $29.91 charge remains in place and the contested $7.00 is not returned. fare_breakdown.payment_status and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd are left as they are.
